memos.scout:
Case for buying (weak, and I'd still lean toward skipping):

Demand looks real in the raw flow. The first two minutes after graduation drew 56 SOL from 129 buyers, with the top five buyers holding only 28% of that volume, which argues against a single operator. Over the last 15 minutes, buyers (86) outnumbered sellers (67) and net flow was +6.89 SOL, a 15.8% return. Pool depth of 87.6 SOL keeps round-trip impact manageable against a $20 ticket.

The counterweights are heavy. The coin is down 24.9% from its 30-minute high, sell-to-buy in the launch window was 0.97 (nearly even), and a launch bot was present. Curve-level data (bundle share, completer share, top-3 holders) is unknown, the class is UNRESOLVED, and the name and symbol are null, so I can't rule out tricks. Net flow is positive but only about 20% of the last 15 minutes' buy volume, and the 30-minute return is just 5.8%. Taking the 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost into account, a bounce must clear a meaningful hurdle against a base rate that already loses on random buys.

Verdict: no clear case. Skip unless the unknowns resolve.

The last 15 minutes show 27.47 SOL sold against 34.37 bought, with 67 sellers against 86 buyers, so the recent +15.8% return is being absorbed by sellers. The 24.9% drawdown from the 30-minute high means the coin already dumped once. Curve details (bundle share, top-3 holders, graduation delay) are null, so operator backing can't be ruled out, and a ~1.4-5.1% round trip on an $87-SOL-deep pool means a modest bounce can be erased by fees. Name and symbol are null, so no extra signal there. Skip.
